_readme: Two floors of a Gurugram office tower. Source deck exports are NOT committed.
No redaction ops: nothing in this set carries a client mark. The reception desk
reads only 'Reception', and the wall graphics are generic.
The building's name appears only in the deck's title slides, which are excluded.
The deck labels one room with a word that may be a family name; it is described
here by what it is - an executive lounge - rather than by that label.

reception.alt: Office reception counter in timber and stone with a fluted dark panel behind
reception.caption: Reception, with a built-in seat to one side rather than a separate waiting room. Indicative viewpoint.

first-floor-plan.alt: Colour-coded first floor office plan showing departments, cabins and a conference room
first-floor-plan.caption: First floor: director rooms and cabins along the glazed edge, departments in the middle, services and lifts at the core.

fourth-floor-plan.alt: Colour-coded fourth floor office plan showing finance and HR departments and a pooja room
fourth-floor-plan.caption: Fourth floor: the same logic repeated — finance and HR departments, conference room, pooja room and an executive lounge.

conference-room-elevations.alt: Conference room drawing sheet with a furniture plan and four wall elevations
conference-room-elevations.caption: The conference room drawn as a plan plus elevations A to D, with every panel, veneer and metal bead called out.

md-cabin-elevations.alt: Managing director's cabin drawing sheet with plan, four elevations and two views
md-cabin-elevations.caption: The MD cabin at the same level of detail, including the safe and the planted corner.

conference-room.alt: Long conference room with a twenty-seat table under a timber ceiling and a globe chandelier
conference-room.caption: The conference room, 21 ft by 14 ft on plan, with rear storage and a screen wall. Indicative viewpoint.

meeting-room.alt: Eight-seat meeting room with a ring pendant light and fluted timber wall
meeting-room.caption: The smaller meeting room off reception, for visitors who do not need the conference table. Indicative viewpoint.

pooja-room.alt: Office pooja room with a backlit niche, lotus artwork and a stone platform
pooja-room.caption: The pooja room: a designed room off the reception end, not a shelf in a corner. Indicative viewpoint.

executive-lounge.alt: Executive lounge with panelled walls, a fluted green screen, armchairs and a low table
executive-lounge.caption: The executive lounge, for the conversation that happens before or after a meeting. Indicative viewpoint.

cafeteria.alt: Office cafeteria with green panelled walls, a long timber table and patterned floor tiles
cafeteria.caption: Cafeteria: one long table rather than scattered fours, so the room seats more and reads as one space. Indicative viewpoint.

pantry.alt: Office pantry with a patterned tile splashback and overhead storage
pantry.caption: The pantry sits separately from the cafeteria, so tea service does not cross a meal. Indicative viewpoint.

workstations-planters.alt: Open-plan workstations screened by planter-topped storage under a linear light
workstations-planters.caption: Workstations screened by planting on the storage line — privacy without partitions. Indicative viewpoint.

workstations-graphics.alt: Workstation bay with a large graphic wall and a textured plaster finish behind
workstations-graphics.caption: Graphics and a textured wall give the deep side of the floor something to look at. Indicative viewpoint.
